2116.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cohesive cluster of large cells with round eccentric nuclei, fine chromatin, small nucleoli, and abundant pale blue foamy cytoplasm with a pale clear zone separated from the nucleus. The cells are larger than plasma cells and lack the clock-face chromatin of plasma cells. Background hematopoietic elements are unremarkable. Findings are consistent with osteoblasts, a normal marrow constituent more frequently seen in aspirates from children or areas of active bone remodeling.

ddx.vs: Plasma cells are smaller with clock-face chromatin and a perinuclear hof immediately adjacent to the nucleus, whereas the osteoblast Golgi zone lies away from the nucleus.
Carcinoma clusters show nuclear pleomorphism, prominent nucleoli, and molding, and are cytokeratin positive, unlike the bland uniform osteoblasts.
Osteoclasts are multinucleated giant cells with many separate nuclei, whereas each osteoblast has a single nucleus.
Mast cells contain dense purple metachromatic granules obscuring the nucleus.

1988.recognize_zh: 低倍淋巴結：箭頭指出被膜下竇與中間竇被一片片淡粉紅色的大型細胞填滿，與周圍深藍色的殘存淋巴組織形成鮮明對比；這種竇內（sinusoidal）生長方式是 anaplastic 型 DLBCL 的特徵，也很像 ALCL 或轉移癌。
features: Lymph node with thin capsule and residual dark blue lymphoid parenchyma
Pale eosinophilic sheets of large cells distending subcapsular and intermediate sinuses (arrows)
Cohesive-appearing sinusoidal aggregates mimicking metastatic carcinoma
Sharp demarcation between tumor-filled sinuses and small lymphocytes
Individual cytologic detail not resolved at this magnification
1988.describe_en: Low-power H&E section of lymph node shows partial involvement by pale sheets of large cells that distend the subcapsular and intermediate sinuses (arrows), sharply demarcated from the residual small lymphocyte-rich parenchyma. The sinusoidal, cohesive-appearing growth pattern mimics metastatic carcinoma. Cytologic detail is not assessable at this magnification. In the context of a B-cell phenotype, findings are consistent with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, anaplastic variant; immunohistochemistry (CD20, PAX5, CD30, ALK, keratin) is required to exclude ALCL and carcinoma.

ddx.dx: ALK-positive or ALK-negative anaplastic large cell lymphoma
ddx.vs: ALCL shares sinusoidal growth and CD30 expression but is a T-cell neoplasm lacking CD20/PAX5, with hallmark cells and ALK or aberrant T-cell markers.
Carcinoma in sinuses is keratin positive and CD45/CD20 negative, whereas lymphoma cells are CD45 and B-cell marker positive.
Melanoma may show pigment and is S100/SOX10 and melan-A positive and CD45 negative.
Sinus histiocytes are bland with abundant pink cytoplasm and small oval nuclei, CD68/CD163 positive, without cytologic atypia or mitoses.

1796.recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中沿著骨小樑表面排成一整列、細胞核偏向一側、細胞質嗜鹼性的豐滿梭形至立方細胞（箭頭），緊貼類骨質邊緣，是造骨細胞（osteoblast）襯覆骨表面的典型表現。
features: Single row of plump cuboidal to spindled cells lining the surface of a bony trabecula (arrows)
Oval, eccentrically placed nuclei with fine chromatin and small nucleoli
Amphophilic to basophilic cytoplasm oriented toward the bone surface
Adjacent lamellar bone with osteocytes in lacunae
Separated marrow space below with a small cluster of hematopoietic cells and red cells
1796.describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows a bony trabecula with osteocytes in lacunae. Its surface is lined by a continuous row of plump cuboidal to spindled cells with eccentric oval nuclei and amphophilic cytoplasm (arrows), consistent with active osteoblasts. The adjacent marrow space contains a small focus of hematopoietic cells without atypia. Findings are consistent with osteoblastic rimming of bone, a normal feature of bone formation and remodeling.

ddx.vs: Carcinoma shows cohesive atypical cells with pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei invading the marrow rather than a single orderly row of bland cells on the bone surface.

ddx.dx: Endothelial cells or bone lining cells
ddx.vs: Inactive lining cells and endothelium are flat and attenuated with thin nuclei, unlike plump cuboidal osteoblasts with abundant cytoplasm.
Osteoclasts are large multinucleated cells sitting in resorption (Howship) lacunae rather than mononuclear cells in a row.

1732.recognize_zh: 抹片中一群大型圓形細胞，細胞質充滿密集、深紫色的嗜鹼性（metachromatic）顆粒並部分遮蓋圓形至卵圓形細胞核，周圍還散落脫出的顆粒，這種成群出現的肥大細胞符合肥大細胞白血病（mast cell leukemia）。
features: Sheet of large round to oval cells packed together, several times the size of red cells
Cytoplasm filled with dense, coarse dark purple metachromatic granules that partly obscure the nucleus
Round to oval centrally placed nuclei with finely granular chromatin; nucleoli not discernible
Numerous extruded granules scattered in the background between cells
Some cells show paler, less granular zones, suggesting partial hypogranularity; image resolution limits fine detail
1732.describe_en: Wright-Giemsa-stained smear shows a cohesive-appearing sheet of large round cells with abundant cytoplasm densely packed with coarse dark purple metachromatic granules, round to oval central nuclei, and numerous extruded granules in the background. Some cells show areas of relative hypogranularity. The specimen source and the proportion of mast cells cannot be determined from this image. Findings are consistent with a marked increase in mast cells; in the appropriate setting, mast cells forming at least 20% of nucleated cells on the aspirate smear support mast cell leukemia, with confirmation by tryptase, CD117, CD25, and KIT D816V testing.

ddx.dx: Basophils (e.g., basophilia in CML or acute basophilic leukemia)
ddx.vs: Basophils are smaller with segmented or lobulated nuclei and water-soluble granules that overlie the nucleus, whereas mast cells are larger with round central nuclei and are strongly CD117 and tryptase positive.
Reactive mast cells are scattered singly, spindled or round, without sheets, and lack CD25/CD2 expression and KIT D816V.
Promyelocytes have azurophilic red-purple granules, bilobed nuclei, and Auer rod bundles, and are MPO strongly positive rather than tryptase positive.
These show a blast population with admixed immature mast cells and lack the dominant mature-appearing granular mast cell sheets; flow and KIT mutation testing help separate them.

1668.recognize_zh: 周邊血液中出現四顆漿細胞樣細胞：核圓且偏向一側、染色質塊狀，細胞質深藍，部分可見核旁淡染區（hof）；周邊血中看到成群漿細胞，是漿細胞白血病的線索。
features: Four circulating plasmacytoid cells in a single field
Eccentrically placed round nuclei with coarsely clumped chromatin
Moderate to abundant deep-blue cytoplasm
Perinuclear clearing (hof) visible in some cells
Background red cells without marked rouleaux in this thin area
1668.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows four circulating plasma cells with eccentric round nuclei, coarsely clumped chromatin and moderately abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm, some with a perinuclear hof. The cells are relatively mature-appearing and uniform. Numerous circulating plasma cells of this type are consistent with plasma cell leukemia (5% or more circulating plasma cells by current criteria); confirmation of a clonal CD138+/CD38+ population with light-chain restriction by flow cytometry is recommended.

ddx.dx: Reactive plasmacytosis (e.g., viral infection, serum sickness)
ddx.vs: Reactive circulating plasma cells are few, accompanied by reactive lymphocytes, and polytypic on flow cytometry.
Shows a spectrum dominated by small lymphocytes and plasmacytoid lymphocytes with a CD19+/CD20+ clonal B-cell population.
Reactive lymphocytes have more central nuclei, less clumped chromatin and lack a well-formed hof.

63364.recognize_zh: 中央一顆淋巴球的細胞質比一般小淋巴球多，且在右側細胞質中可見少數粗大的紫紅色嗜天青顆粒（azurophilic granules），這是大顆粒淋巴球（large granular lymphocyte）的特徵。
features: Single lymphocyte roughly 1.3-1.5 times the diameter of a red cell
Round to slightly irregular nucleus with condensed, clumped chromatin and no visible nucleolus
Moderate amount of pale blue cytoplasm, eccentrically distributed toward the right
A few coarse, discrete azurophilic (red-purple) cytoplasmic granules
Background red cells include many oval forms (mild ovalocytosis); rare platelets
63364.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells with a notable proportion of oval forms and a single lymphocyte in the center of the field. The lymphocyte is slightly larger than a small resting lymphocyte, with a round nucleus with mature clumped chromatin and a moderate amount of pale blue cytoplasm containing a few coarse azurophilic granules. No nucleoli, cytoplasmic basophilia or blast features are seen. Findings are consistent with a large granular (cytotoxic T or NK) lymphocyte; a persistent absolute increase would warrant flow cytometry and TCR clonality studies to exclude T-LGL leukemia.

ddx.vs: Reactive lymphocytes are larger with abundant cytoplasm that shows peripheral basophilia and scalloping around red cells, usually without discrete azurophilic granules.
Monocytes are larger with a folded or kidney-shaped nucleus, lacy chromatin and grey-blue vacuolated cytoplasm with very fine, dust-like granules.
Morphology of individual cells is identical; the leukemia requires a sustained LGL count (usually >2 x 10^9/L) with clonal CD3+CD8+CD57+ cells on flow cytometry and TCR rearrangement.

60932.recognize_zh: 紅血球之間散布幾個遠小於紅血球（約其四分之一大小）、無核、帶紫色細顆粒的小點，就是正常大小的血小板（normal platelets）。
features: A few small anucleate platelets, roughly one-quarter to one-third the diameter of a red cell
Platelets show fine purple (alpha) granules with scant pale cytoplasm
Platelets are dispersed singly without clumping
Background normocytic, normochromic red cells with normal central pallor and minimal poikilocytosis
No leukocytes in this low-to-intermediate power field
60932.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic, normochromic red cells with preserved central pallor and no significant poikilocytosis. Scattered small platelets are present singly, each much smaller than a red cell, with fine purple granules and scant pale cytoplasm. No platelet clumps, large or giant platelets, or leukocytes are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with normal platelet morphology; platelet number should be assessed over multiple fields.

ddx.vs: Large platelets exceed about 4 micrometers, approaching half a red cell diameter, whereas these are clearly small.

ddx.dx: Red cell inclusions (Howell-Jolly or Pappenheimer bodies)
ddx.vs: Inclusions lie within the red cell outline, whereas these platelets are separate from red cells in the background.
Precipitate forms irregular dark refractile dots in variable planes, lacking the granular center and pale cytoplasm of platelets.

60292.recognize_zh: 這群細胞核呈圓形、位於中央，細胞質從深藍色（嗜鹼性幼紅血球）逐步變成灰藍色、核也漸濃縮變小（多染性幼紅血球），同一視野呈現紅血球系列的成熟階段（erythroid precursors）。
features: Cluster of round cells with central round nuclei and smooth cell borders
Earlier forms with coarsely granular chromatin and a rim of deeply basophilic, agranular cytoplasm (basophilic normoblasts)
Smaller later forms with condensed, dark nuclei and gray-blue cytoplasm (polychromatophilic normoblasts)
Admixed granulocytic cells, including a granulated myeloid precursor and a segmented neutrophil
Several stripped or smudged nuclei and a marrow particle edge in the background
60292.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows clusters of erythroid precursors at different stages of maturation. Basophilic normoblasts have round nuclei with coarsely granular chromatin and deeply basophilic, agranular cytoplasm, while smaller polychromatophilic normoblasts show more condensed nuclei and gray-blue cytoplasm. A granulated myeloid precursor, a segmented neutrophil and several smudged nuclei are also present. Maturation appears orderly without megaloblastic change or multinucleation. Findings are consistent with normal maturing erythroid precursors.

ddx.vs: Lymphocytes have denser, smudgier chromatin and pale sky-blue cytoplasm, unlike the round crisply clumped nuclei and intensely basophilic cytoplasm of erythroid precursors.
Plasma cells have eccentric nuclei with a perinuclear hof, whereas these cells have centrally placed nuclei without a hof.
Megaloblasts are larger with open sieve-like chromatin that lags behind cytoplasmic hemoglobinization, which is not seen in these orderly maturing cells.

132.recognize_zh: 乳房脂肪組織旁有纖維化背景與濃密淋巴漿細胞浸潤，其間散在胞質豐富淡染、核呈泡狀且核仁明顯的大型組織球；高倍下組織球胞質內含完整淋巴球或漿細胞（emperipolesis，箭頭），S-100 強陽性並清楚勾勒出被吞入的細胞輪廓，符合結外 Rosai-Dorfman disease。
features: Large polygonal histiocytes with abundant pale, finely vacuolated to foamy eosinophilic cytoplasm and indistinct cell borders
Round vesicular nuclei with fine chromatin and small distinct central nucleoli
Emperipolesis: intact lymphocytes, plasma cells and a neutrophil/eosinophil-like cell within histiocyte cytoplasm (arrows)
Strong nuclear and cytoplasmic S-100 staining of histiocytes, with engulfed cells appearing as unstained halos
Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in a fibrotic/sclerotic stroma extending around a muscular vessel and into adjacent adipose tissue
Numerous plasma cells highlighted by IHC; kappa and lambda ISH show a polytypic plasma cell population
132.describe_en: Core biopsy of breast shows a cellular, partly sclerotic lesion adjacent to mature adipose tissue, composed of sheets of large pale histiocytes admixed with a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate and extending around a thick-walled vessel. At high power, the histiocytes have abundant pale to foamy cytoplasm and round vesicular nuclei with small nucleoli, and many contain intact lymphocytes and plasma cells within their cytoplasm (emperipolesis). No significant nuclear atypia, mitotic activity, necrosis or cohesive epithelial clusters are seen in these fields. The histiocytes are strongly S-100 positive, outlining the engulfed cells. Plasma cells are abundant, and kappa and lambda in situ hybridization show a polytypic pattern. Findings are consistent with extranodal Rosai-Dorfman disease involving the breast.

ddx.vs: IgG4-RD shows storiform fibrosis and obliterative phlebitis without large S-100-positive emperipolesis-containing histiocytes, although RDD may also contain increased IgG4-positive plasma cells.
LCH cells are smaller with grooved, reniform nuclei, are CD1a and langerin positive, lack emperipolesis and are typically accompanied by eosinophils.
Granular cell tumor is also S-100 positive but has coarse eosinophilic PAS-positive cytoplasmic granules, lacks emperipolesis and lacks the heavy lymphoplasmacytic background.
Carcinoma cells are keratin and GATA3 positive, often show intracytoplasmic lumina and single-file infiltration, and are S-100 negative without emperipolesis.

132.stain: H&E; IHC: S-100, plasma cell IHC; ISH: kappa/lambda
captions: H&E low power: lymphoplasmacytic and histiocytic infiltrate with sclerosis around a muscular vessel, adjacent fat
H&E medium power: dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate admixed with clusters of large pale histiocytes
H&E high power: large histiocyte with vesicular nucleus engulfing intact inflammatory cells (emperipolesis, arrow)
H&E high power: pale histiocyte containing multiple intact lymphocytes (emperipolesis, arrow)
S-100 IHC: strong staining of histiocytes with engulfed cells seen as negative halos (arrows)
S-100 IHC high power: large positive histiocyte containing several unstained lymphocytes (arrow)
IHC for plasma cells (likely IgG/IgG4) at low power: numerous positive plasma cells among histiocytes
Same plasma cell IHC at higher power: strongly positive plasma cells in a background of negative histiocytes
Kappa ISH: numerous positive plasma cells
Lambda ISH: fewer but readily identified positive plasma cells, supporting a polytypic population

68.recognize_zh: 骨髓切片可見成片的大型未成熟細胞，核呈卵圓或凹折、染色質細緻、有核仁，取代正常造血；抹片中母細胞（blast）量多，部分細胞質灰藍、核有凹摺，呈單核球樣分化。形態只能判定為急性骨髓性白血病（AML），雙等位 CEBPA 突變需靠分子檢測確認。
features: Hypercellular marrow with sheets of large immature cells effacing normal hematopoiesis (biopsy)
Blasts with oval to folded/indented nuclei, fine open chromatin, and visible nucleoli
Aspirate blasts with moderate basophilic to grey-blue cytoplasm, some with perinuclear hof, a subset with monocytoid nuclear folding
Residual scattered megakaryocytes, including small hypolobated forms, and hemosiderin-laden macrophages
Peripheral blood shows occasional circulating blast and mature neutrophils with small nuclear appendages; background RBCs with crenation
No Auer rods, cup-like nuclei, or abnormal promyelocytes evident in these fields
68.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows occasional circulating blasts with high N:C ratio and deeply basophilic cytoplasm, along with scattered mature neutrophils. The bone marrow core biopsy is hypercellular for age, with interstitial to sheet-like infiltration by large immature mononuclear cells with oval to indented nuclei, vesicular chromatin, and small nucleoli; residual megakaryocytes and hemosiderin-laden macrophages are present. The aspirate smear contains numerous blasts with moderate grey-blue cytoplasm, some showing nuclear folding suggestive of monocytic differentiation; Auer rods are not identified in these fields. Findings are consistent with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia; morphology does not specify the genetic subtype, and the reported biallelic CEBPA mutation requires molecular confirmation.

ddx.vs: NPM1-mutated AML may show cup-like (fish-mouth) nuclear invaginations and often a normal karyotype as well, so separation from CEBPA-mutated AML requires molecular testing or aberrant cytoplasmic NPM1 immunostaining.
Monocytic features overlap, but the diagnosis of a genetically defined entity rests on detecting biallelic CEBPA (bZIP) mutation rather than on nuclear folding or nonspecific esterase alone.

ddx.dx: Post-transplant regenerating marrow with left shift
ddx.vs: Regeneration shows orderly maturation with promyelocytes and myelocytes outnumbering blasts, whereas here sheets of blasts efface the marrow and blasts are numerous on the aspirate.

ddx.dx: Therapy-related myeloid neoplasm/MDS with excess blasts
ddx.vs: MDS-EB has <20% blasts with prominent multilineage dysplasia, whereas the aspirate here is dominated by blasts exceeding the AML threshold.

captions: Peripheral blood: circulating blast with deeply basophilic cytoplasm
Peripheral blood: two mature neutrophils, one with small nuclear appendages
Peripheral blood: granulated leukocyte with folded nucleus
Core biopsy, low power: hypercellular marrow with diffuse immature infiltrate
Core biopsy, medium power: sheets of blasts with hemosiderin-laden macrophages
Core biopsy, high power: blasts with vesicular chromatin and nucleoli
Core biopsy, high power: paratrabecular blast infiltrate
Core biopsy, high power: blasts with a small hypolobated megakaryocyte
Aspirate: numerous blasts with basophilic cytoplasm
Aspirate: blasts with grey-blue cytoplasm and folded nuclei (monocytoid features)

4.recognize_zh: 皮膚切片真皮被單一形態的中型未成熟細胞瀰漫浸潤，細胞在膠原束間穿插排列，核染色質細、可見小核仁與核分裂；在已知慢性骨髓性腫瘤病史下，免疫染色呈骨髓系顆粒狀胞質陽性，支持髓外骨髓腫瘤（leukemia cutis）。
features: Dense, diffuse dermal infiltrate extending up to a thin, largely spared zone beneath an intact epidermis
Monotonous medium-sized immature cells with round to slightly irregular nuclei, fine chromatin and small nucleoli
Tumor cells dissect between and single-file around collagen bundles
Frequent mitoses and scattered apoptotic bodies
Unlabeled IHC shows weak granular cytoplasmic/membranous positivity in tumor cells with a negative epidermis
4.describe_en: Skin biopsy shows a dense, diffuse dermal infiltrate beneath an intact epidermis, with tumor cells dissecting between collagen bundles. At high power the infiltrate consists of monotonous medium-sized immature cells with fine chromatin, small nucleoli, scant to moderate cytoplasm, frequent mitoses and apoptotic bodies; no epidermotropism is identified. An immunostain (marker not labeled in the image) shows weak granular cytoplasmic positivity in the neoplastic cells while the epidermis is negative, in keeping with a myeloid immunophenotype described for this case. In the setting of a known chronic myeloid neoplasm, findings are consistent with extramedullary myeloid tumor (leukemia cutis), representing blast transformation.

ddx.vs: DLBCL cells are larger with vesicular chromatin and prominent nucleoli and are CD20/PAX5-positive and MPO/CD33/lysozyme-negative.
BPDCN shows similar blastic dermal sheets but is CD4+, CD56+, CD123+, TCF4+ and MPO/lysozyme-negative.
Lymphoblastic lymphoma expresses TdT with CD3 or CD79a/PAX5 and lacks myeloid markers such as MPO.

ddx.dx: Merkel cell carcinoma or other small round cell tumor
ddx.vs: Merkel cell carcinoma has salt-and-pepper chromatin with nuclear molding and is CK20 dot-like and neuroendocrine-marker positive but CD45-negative.

captions: H&E low power: diffuse dermal infiltrate beneath intact epidermis
H&E high power: medium-sized blasts with fine chromatin dissecting collagen, mitoses
IHC (unlabeled): weak granular cytoplasmic positivity in tumor cells, negative epidermis

66116.recognize_zh: 這是左眼眼底照片（視神經盤在畫面左側），在視神經盤上顳側可見一塊邊界清楚的紅色視網膜內出血，上緣帶淡白色弧形反光；白血病患者出現此類出血需考慮 Roth spot，但本圖中央白心並不明顯。
features: Color fundus photograph of the left eye with the optic disc at the left edge of the image
Single well-demarcated, oval to boat-shaped red intraretinal hemorrhage superotemporal to the optic disc along the superior arcade
Faint pale arc at the upper margin of the hemorrhage; a distinct central white core is not clearly seen
Optic disc margins appear sharp; retinal vessels are prominent without obvious sheathing
Central bright reflex near the macula is a photographic light artifact; image digitally enhanced (watermark)
66116.describe_en: Color fundus photograph of the left eye shows a single well-circumscribed intraretinal hemorrhage superotemporal to the optic disc, adjacent to the superior vascular arcade, with a faint pale rim along its upper edge. A definite central white fibrin-platelet core is not clearly resolved in this enhanced image, and no additional hemorrhages, cotton-wool spots or disc edema are evident; the central whitish patch is a light reflex artifact. The title describes chronic myeloid leukemia while the case is filed under CMML, and the ocular finding itself does not distinguish these entities. In a patient with leukemia, the hemorrhage is compatible with a Roth spot, reflecting anemia, thrombocytopenia and/or leukostasis.

ddx.vs: These show multiple dot-blot or flame hemorrhages with microaneurysms, hard exudates or arteriolar narrowing rather than an isolated white-centered hemorrhage in a cytopenic patient.
The fundus lesion is identical; separation depends on blood cultures, echocardiography and the blood count rather than ophthalmoscopic appearance.
Vein occlusion produces numerous flame hemorrhages in the drainage territory of the occluded vein with venous dilation and tortuosity, not a single focal hemorrhage.
Leukemic infiltrates appear as elevated grayish-white nodules or perivascular sheathing rather than a flat red hemorrhage.

4228.recognize_zh: 大小正常的紅血球內有兩個成熟的滋養體/早期裂殖體，胞內含深褐黑色瘧色素（hemozoin）與數個染色質點；感染的紅血球沒有變大、也沒有 Schüffner 小點，符合惡性瘧原蟲（P. falciparum）。
features: Two parasitized red cells containing compact mature trophozoites/early schizonts with dark brown-black hemozoin pigment
Parasites show several chromatin dots and bluish cytoplasm filling part of the host cell
Infected red cells are normal in size, without Schüffner stippling
Background of densely packed, uninfected red cells; no gametocytes or white cells in field
4228.describe_en: Smear from a bone marrow aspirate preparation (thin, erythrocyte-rich area) shows two parasitized red cells containing pigmented mature trophozoites/early schizonts with coarse dark hemozoin and several chromatin dots. The infected erythrocytes are not enlarged and lack Schüffner stippling. No gametocytes are present in this field, and marrow cellular elements are not included. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium falciparum infection with mature (pigmented) asexual forms, which are typically sequestered in tissue and marrow rather than circulating.

ddx.vs: Vivax and ovale mature forms enlarge the host red cell and show Schüffner stippling, whereas these infected cells are normal-sized without stippling.
P. malariae shows band-form trophozoites and rosette schizonts in small red cells, and species confirmation may require PCR when only pigmented trophozoites are seen.
Babesia lacks hemozoin pigment and schizonts and may form Maltese-cross tetrads.
